fields.AN_Notes: Narrative review that builds the five-component framework Reflexive Prompt Engineering (section 1.2). General_Guidance: 'prompts can be intentionally crafted or augmented with instructions to avoid bias' (3.1.3). ICL as balanced, randomly ordered few-shot examples and counterfactual attribute flipping (3.1.1), Thought_Generation as chain-of-thought with ethical checkpoints (3.1.2), Self_Criticism as a separate verification step 'Plan verification questions to fact-check this draft' (3.1.2). Object_of_Critique: chain-of-thought explanations as an 'illusion of transparency' (3.1.2). AN_Bias_Axes None: gender and race appear only as illustrative attributes in cited practitioner sources ('person' instead of gender-specific terms, flipping gender or race), not as an axis the work analyses. AN_Harm_Types None: stereotyping and the Gemini misrepresentation incident are named from cited sources and news reports, the framework does not establish a harm mechanism of its own. Mitigation stays Proposed, the work recommends debiasing via prompt design, documentation, stakeholder involvement and human oversight without its own evaluation. AN_Task None: no professional task, the framework is general.

fields.AN_Notes: Experiment on Flan-PaLM 540B with a people-diversity dataset (105 professions) and a culture-diversity dataset, automated entropy and max-gap metrics and human side-by-side ratings. Prompting techniques: CCSV combines self-critique and revision (Self_Criticism) with sampling several drafts and self-voting (Ensembling); baselines include 5-shot exemplars (ICL), zero- and few-shot chain-of-thought (Thought_Generation) and the 0-shot diversity instruction 'Write AI model's response to the user question such that it has diversity' (General_Guidance), which failed. Evaluated: CCSV outperforms all baselines on automated and human evaluation. Language_Culture is coded through the culture-diversity task (section 6.2), evaluated by human raters only. AN_Gender_Understanding Non_Binary_Inclusive is a boundary decision: the gender attribute takes the values male, female and other from a knowledge graph, and the authors state that 'other' is not an ideal stand-in for genders beyond male and female (Limitations); the analysis does carry a category beyond the binary. Prompting also serves as Research_Instrument through the people-seeking templates. AN_Task None: general LLM evaluation without a professional task.

fields.AN_Notes: Narrative review of AI and machine learning in social work: predictive risk analytics in child welfare, mental-health chatbots, NLP for case notes, automated case management, AI in social work education. AN_Bias_Axes Race_Ethnicity: the review develops the racial overrepresentation of families in child-abuse risk prediction as its own worked example (4.1) and returns to the Allegheny case (4.1.1). Socioeconomic (housing vouchers) and Language_Culture (English-only chatbots) appear only in the list of cited cases in 4.1.1 and are left uncoded; gender appears only in an enumeration. AN_Harm_Types Indirect_Discrimination: the own argument in 4.1 places the disadvantage in risk scores learned from historical data, an allocation decision through a proxy rather than the attribute itself. Mitigation Proposed: diverse and inclusive datasets (Pre_Processing), auditing, transparency, involvement of social workers and community members, AI training (Organisational_Process). Source-quality note: several references are implausible for their claims, e.g. an AI review on net-zero building design cited for NLP case documentation and a paper on deep-learning loop execution cited for predictive analytics in social work; this does not change the publication type but limits the evidential weight of the cited case studies.

fields.AN_Notes: Reflective empirical account of co-creation workshops of the Horizon Europe MAMMOth project with marginalized groups (women at risk of social exclusion, young people, ethnic minorities, migrants, LGBTQI+ early career researchers), each opened by a training module on AI bias, feeding user and research requirements of an AI bias toolkit. AN_Task Other_Task: AI-based home loan decisions, biometric identity verification and academic citation search as use cases. AN_Bias_Axes: Gender through the gender-bias training examples (stereotypical parent roles in generative AI, gendered job endings in Google Translate), Race_Ethnicity through postal codes as race proxy in the toolkit, Religion and Physical_Appearance through the ranked facial attributes for ID verification (hijabs and turbans, piercings and tattoos). Sexual orientation and migration describe participant groups only and are left uncoded. AN_Harm_Types: Stereotyping from the training examples, Indirect_Discrimination from the proxy bias the toolkit addresses. Mitigation Demonstrated: training within participatory co-creation was applied and reflected through facilitator and participant feedback, without a reported assessment of bias reduction. Gender is treated through examples and a participant group without a stated understanding, hence Absent and Unclear. Soziale_Arbeit teilweise: participants include recipients of social protection services and domestic violence victims recruited via civil society organizations, but no social work practice is addressed.
